newsitem.title: USA: Texas wheat condition improves, snow beneficial.
newsitem.headline: Texas wheat condition improves, snow beneficial.

text.p: The condition of the Texas wheat crop improved in the week to Sunday, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
"Snowfall was not heavy enough for much benefit in the Northern High Plains. However, heavier amounts in the Southern High Plains were beneficial," the report said.
Statewide, wheat was rated 70 percent of normal, up from 60 percent a week earlier and 43 percent last year.
"Irrigated fields in the Plains continued to make good progress with dryland fields needing moisture," the weekly report said.

Wheat was rated nine percent excellent, 40 percent good, 34 percent fair, 15 percent poor and two percent very poor. The comparative figures a week earlier were two percent, 28 percent, 44 percent, 23 percent and three percent.
Livestock conditions remained good across the state.
Range and pasture conditions were rated five percent excellent, 23 percent good, 36 percent fair, 25 percent poor and 11 percent very poor.
